opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write (role does not own Payroll, so no admin). Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB for E019 (Eric Woods): contractor, basic security training. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role. Contractor with basic training max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: the security DB note indicates Eric Woods is a contractor with basic security training, while the other note claims full-time. Per policy, a contractor with basic training has max access of read for Payroll (write requires advanced security training; admin is never allowed for contractors). The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: read.
